items.query: Block outgoing shipments when there is not enough stock on hand
From a delivery order, users should be able to see the related invoices
Lot numbers should be generated automatically when receiving goods
Move all products from shelf A to shelf B in one operation
Reopen a cancelled transfer so it can be edited and processed again
When invoicing a sales order based on delivered quantities, each invoice must be traceable to the delivery it covers
The main warehouse must never ship more than it has on hand, but one consignment location should still allow outgoing moves even when its quantities are not yet reconciled.

After rushed deliveries, accounting keeps finding items with on-hand quantity below zero; the system should refuse to validate such transfers, except for the spare-parts product category that is only counted at month end.
When opening an invoice, accounting needs to see which stock transfers it covers and which stock moves each invoice line corresponds to.

When emptying a shelf for maintenance, the storekeeper wants to create an internal transfer without typing each product: pick the source shelf and the system fills the transfer with everything currently stored there.
All products in the fresh-food category must get lot numbers generated automatically at receipt, without enabling it product by product, and only for the vendor receipt operation type.
From the on-hand stock list, the storekeeper wants to select a few stock lines and move only those quantities to another location right away.

On the inventory overview, each internal transfer type should have a button to move on-hand stock from one location to another, and the warehouse manager decides per operation type whether the button is shown.
A user cancelled a customer delivery by mistake; we need to bring that same delivery back and process it instead of creating a new one with a different reference.
When an invoice is created from a partially delivered sales order, each invoice line should automatically record the deliveries it bills, without accounting picking them by hand.
When a customer returns goods and accounting creates a credit note from the original invoice, the credit note lines must be linked to the corresponding return stock moves.
The production department needs to send the warehouse a request for materials stating product, quantity and delivery location, and then follow the transfers created for that request.
A shift leader wants to submit one request covering several products at once, sharing the same warehouse, destination location and needed date, and follow the overall status of the whole request.

When a department requests goods and enough unreserved quantity is already available at the destination location, that stock should be used directly without triggering replenishment from the central warehouse; this rule applies company-wide.
One transfer may carry goods for several material requests; the manager needs to know, for each request, how much has been delivered, how much is still in progress and how much was cancelled.
